content: Coronin-6, also referred to as coronin-like protein E (Clipin-E), is a protein encoded by the CORO6 gene in humans. This protein is a member of the coronin family, which is known for its role in binding to actin. The CORO6 gene is located on chromosome 17, specifically at the cytogenetic band 17p11.2. The gene is highly conserved across eukaryotic species, ranging from animals to fungi. Expression Profile Based on expressed sequence tag (EST) profiling, CORO6 is expressed at high levels in the larynx, nerves, and muscles. Additionally, elevated expression of CORO6 has been observed in breast (mammary gland) tumors. During human development, CORO6 expression is particularly high at the blastocyst stage and in adult tissues. Transcript Variants The CORO6 gene undergoes alternative splicing, producing 10 distinct mRNA variants. These variants are aligned from the 5' to 3' ends on a virtual genome, where introns are minimized for visualization. Exon sizes are proportional to their actual lengths, while intron heights reflect the number of cDNAs supporting each intron. Introns of the same color are identical, while those of different colors are distinct. Transcripts encoding functional proteins are marked in pink, while partial or non-functional proteins are marked in yellow. Upstream open reading frames (uORFs) are shown in green. The presence of 5' caps or 3' polyadenylation (poly-A) flags indicates the completeness of the transcripts. The CORO6 gene contains 21 distinct GT-AG introns and has three probable alternative promoters, as well as validated alternative polyadenylation sites. Protein Structure The CORO6 protein sequence includes WD-40 repeats, which are structural motifs commonly found in eukaryotic proteins. These WD-40 domains serve as adaptor or regulatory modules in various cellular processes, including signal transduction, pre-mRNA processing, and cytoskeletal assembly. The WD-40 domain typically terminates with a WD dipeptide at its C-terminus and is approximately 40 amino acids in length. The structure of CORO6 has been predicted using the Phyre2 program, revealing a high degree of similarity to the crystal structure of murine coronin-1. Approximately 390 residues, accounting for 83% of the CORO6 protein sequence, have been modeled with 100% confidence based on the highest-scoring template. Homology Paralogs CORO6 has several paralogs in humans, including CORO1A, CORO1B, CORO1C, CORO2A, CORO2B, and CORO7. Among these, CORO1A and CORO1B are the most closely related to CORO6 based on sequence comparisons. Orthologs The CORO6 gene is highly conserved across a wide range of organisms, from vertebrates to fungi. Representative species from these groups have been identified to highlight the evolutionary conservation of this gene. Clinical Significance Clinical studies utilizing microarray analyses have demonstrated that CORO6 is positively associated with the allergic response of nasal epithelium to house dust mite allergens in vitro. This suggests a potential role for CORO6 in allergic reactions and immune responses. Model Organisms To study the function of CORO6, a conditional knockout mouse line, designated as Coro6tm1e(EUCOMM)Wtsi, was developed at the Wellcome Trust Sanger Institute. Both male and female mice underwent a standardized phenotypic screening process to assess the effects of CORO6 deletion. Additional in-depth immunological phenotyping was also performed to further investigate the role of this gene.
